One side is the team that knows what’s coming and why adding more vehicles is good for the long term (I’ll come back to the team in a bit).
The other side is the investor that wants to know that the team they are investing in has their back and are making wise decisions. When an investor sees another mint announced right after a previous mint it tends to throw up a red flag. “Wait a second, what’s this all about? Why didn’t I know about this before? Won’t this be too many vehicles without having a game already? Will they just keep producing vehicles, causing the prices to stay down?” So then the investor pauses and thinks to themselves, “okay check for the use case differences”… but when looking the use cases have been left at “there may be this benefit or that benefit but no guarantees” - except for that the Sprinter does have a second seat - yet rental service was still TBD. They also hear that rarities may not play any difference and are told that is due to not wanting a pay to win mindset - yet, they also see that people are offered pay for resources in game (which is partially pay to win). The investor who doesn’t have clear details and a sort of vagueness about the game freaks out. Now with that said…

Public (launchpad) - 25% Unlocked on Listing then 25% every 30 days - Token Price @ .00365

I have not been a part of many NFT Mints. However, I have minted an NFT with the assistance of Adam Dean. It was an NFT to commentate the 1 year anniversary of Cardano Project Catalyst Fund1 .

From my admittedly uninformed vantage point, I have noticed that some folks are suffering with Cross Project Language Disorder. 

CPLD causes a sufferer to believe that a word used by one project means the same thing that (they think) it means in another project.

Language has been a problem for humans for millennia, and we keep expanding our reach and potential for mis-understanding. 

The only cure for CPLD is documentation PLUS reading of said documentation.

Rarity in my mind means nothing more than that there are few of a thing. As in there are only 1,000, or 10, or 1 of that thing.

I think ascribing any more meaning to that word is getting into the danger zone.
CPLD appears to have folks thinking that Rarity in fact means lots of other things. Thinks like immunity from market forces, and thereby preventing the CPLD sufferer from experiencing financial loss.

My advice is to do a check on yourself every time that you see a word that you have seen in another project, and ask yourself if you are 100% certain that in Cornucopias it means what you think it means. 
ESPECIALLY if your thought has any financial implications.

Essentially, anything past the presale is demand driven. The demand of a token for a game before the game releases and actually utilizes it as a liquidity tool or implements a staking mechanism just rises and falls to greater degree with the market. For example, gods unchained released their gods token and it started at a price of 6-8 dollars after the presale. Now it’s trading for ~$1 because you can use Ethereum for everything that gods tokens can be used for. There’s no demand for the token, so price just tanked as more token unlocks occurred over time. Another example is illuvium. “Early investors” that bought it on market are now down 80%. I personally have learnt that:
If you aren’t part of the public sale or initial coin offering, the demand drivers for the coin will be very very low and more susceptible to downside risks than upside until there is built-in demand drivers past just hype. I will personally learn from these mistakes, and seeing as I missed the presale of copi, I will wait until the demand drivers for the token are announced/implemented. (edited)

I’ll go ahead and comment on the 2nd mint/people being bothered (I hope this helps)…

What’s the problem?
Most people are saying a 2nd close mint is a problem, but I don’t think that’s the main problem. So, what is? I think it’s actually the lack of clarity the community has between vehicles.
-Why should I own the Sprinter over the Javelin or vice versa?
    -The Sprinter came out 1st but will be slower and cost more. It will have a second seat though. Okay… so how important is that 2nd seat? Is it more                 important than having speed in game?
    -We don’t know the price of the sprinter. Suppose it’s 60ada… will the Sprinter be at least twice as good in game?
-Since a game is “what’s being sold”, people aren’t looking at the vehicles as NFTs - they are looking at them as usable items - so they want to see use case per vehicle - that’s how they are valuing and comparing each usable item that the game will produce.

…but the details are coming… 
The problem with this is that if you announce two of a similar asset at nearly the same time, the details should be out for both before selling either. It’d be like Apple selling a MacBook and then a week later saying “we have a new model that will be faster and cheap then what you just bought. We aren’t revealing all the details quite yet” - I think it’d cause quite the stir… now on the other hand, they could release 3 models at once and outline the specs and no-one would put up a fuss and quite the opposite - it’d be like “thank you for thinking of everyone”

*Note: I don’t believe there is anything wrong about teasing an asset and it’s actually great… as long as it’s either sold a good while later or is clear at the time that another similar asset will be coming out but with “these distinct differences”... now please see my next comment

*Please note that I absolutely love the team and I am heavily invested in this project. I believe fully that they are professional and everything will be just fine and the game will be unbelievable. I think as Josh said, they are building a community that understands their vision. So, the 2nd mint being close was expected to be taken as “you can trust the team, they have your best interest in mind.” - And I think this is the part that those who are fearful are struggling over.
